questions.question: What computer do you use day to day?
Do you have a computer that stays on ALL the time?
questions.help: This means a machine that is awake even when nobody is touching it, like a Mac mini or a desktop in a closet that never sleeps. Your everyday laptop does NOT count: it sleeps when the lid closes.

options.label: Yes, a desktop or Mac mini that never sleeps
No, just my laptop and phone

questions.question: Where should your brain run?
questions.help: Both answers are YOUR infrastructure; there is no "we host it for you" option, because we never hold your memory. The choice is whether it lives on hosting you rent or on a Mac you already own, and it changes which accounts you sign up for. Your texts and Apple Notes do not depend on this choice: they need a Mac, but a Mac helper can feed a cloud brain just as well. Neither path sets that up for you yet.

options.label: In the cloud, on hosting in my name
options.hint: Your own Railway and Supabase accounts, about $20 a month. Reachable from your phone with every device of yours switched off. Most people pick this.

options.label: On my own always-on Mac mini
options.hint: A Mac mini (or another desktop Mac) that never sleeps. A MacBook does not work for this: it sleeps when the lid closes, and a sleeping brain is unreachable. No monthly hosting bill, nothing leaves your house except what you connect. Needs two free accounts — Tailscale to reach it, Cloudflare R2 to hold the nightly backup off the machine.

connectionsNote: Your brain reaches sources like Slack and Google through small "connector apps" — the registered doorway a service uses to grant access. During setup you can let us host those doorways where supported, or create them yourself with guided steps. Either way your data, your database, and your brain stay yours: we only ever host the doorway, never what passes through it.

cloud.cost: About $20 a month for hosting, plus a few dollars a month of AI usage. Your database starts on Supabase's free tier and only costs anything (about $25 a month) if you outgrow it. No hardware to buy, and it answers your phone with every device of yours switched off.
cloud.ownership: Every account is in your name, every bill is yours, and so is the data. We never hold your accounts, your credentials, or your memory — you can cancel any of it without asking us.
notYet: Your texts (iMessage) and your Apple Notes CAN come into your brain, and setup covers it: the helper authenticates with an append-only token your brain mints for that Mac, so no password of yours goes on the machine and you can revoke it in one line. Either way this needs a Mac in the house — that is where the messages and notes physically live — but it does NOT need your brain to run on one: a small helper on the Mac ships them to your brain wherever it lives, cloud included. There is no Windows or Android path for texts.

mac-mini.cost: No monthly hosting bill: the always-on Mac you already own does the work, and its database lives on the same machine, so there is no database bill either. (The setup does offer a hosted database instead if you prefer one — that becomes its own signup and its own cost.) You still pay a few dollars a month of AI usage, and the machine has to stay awake and plugged in: when it sleeps, your brain is unreachable.
